A.explanation: The horizontal axis is distance $x$, so the crest-to-crest distance is wavelength $\lambda$, not period $T$.

B.explanation: The $\lambda$ label is on the correct $d$-$x$ axis, but $a$ is drawn from crest to trough which is $2a$, not amplitude.

C.explanation: The horizontal axis is time $t$, so the crest-to-crest interval is period $T$, not wavelength $\lambda$.

D.explanation: The $d$-$t$ crest-to-crest interval is correctly labelled $T$ and $a$ is correctly shown from $d=0$ to the crest.

hints: Notice whether the horizontal axis is distance $x$ or time $t$ - $\lambda$ can only be read from a $d$-$x$ graph and $T$ can only be read from a $d$-$t$ graph.
Recall that amplitude $a$ is the maximum displacement from equilibrium, measured from the $d=0$ line to a crest, not from crest to trough.
Check each horizontal double-arrow: it must join two identical points such as crest to next crest on the correct axis to represent one $\lambda$ or one $T$.
walkthrough: Graphs A and B plot $d$ against $x$ at one instant, so the repeating length is wavelength $\lambda$. Graphs C and D plot $d$ against $t$ at fixed $x$, so the repeating time is period $T$.
Amplitude $a$ is the peak height above equilibrium, from the $d=0$ line to the top of a crest. The full crest-to-trough distance is $2a$.
Graph A fails because it labels the $d$-$x$ repeat as $T$. Graph B has $\lambda$ on the correct axis but shows $a$ spanning crest to trough.
Graph C fails because it labels the $d$-$t$ repeat as $\lambda$, even though its $a$ arrow from $0$ to crest is correct.
Graph D shows $T$ as the crest-to-crest time on the $d$-$t$ graph and shows $a$ from $d=0$ to the crest. Both definitions are satisfied. This is option D
